texts.preamble: Shri J.Sarvana vs Shri Ashwatha Gowda on 25 April, 2019 In The Court Of Iii Addl.Judge And Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Court Of Small Causes Bengaluru (Scch-18) Dated: This the 25th day of April 2019 Present: Sri.Mahantesh S.Dargad B.Sc., LL.B.,(Spl) Iii Addl. Judge & Member, Mact Court Of Small Causes, Bengaluru. M.V.C.No.7496/2017 Petitioner Shri J.Sarvana, Son of Jayaraj, Aged about 29 years, Residing at Vinoba Nagar, Sanitorium, Kolar. (By Pleader Shri T.V.Ramesh) V/s. Respondents 1.Shri Ashwatha Gowda, Son of Narayanappa, Major, Residing at Bangavadi Village, Gandlahalli Post, Srinivasapura Taluk, Kolar District. (By Pleader Shri G.N.Prasad) 2 Scch-18 Mvc 7496/2017 2.The Iffco -Tokio General Insurance Co.Ltd., Shri Shanthi Towers, 5th Floor, No.141, 3rd Main, East of Ngef Layout, Kasthuri Nagar, Bengaluru-560 043. (By Pleader Shri Krishna Kishore) J U D G M E N T
texts.facts: The petitioner has filed this claim petition U/S.166 of M.V. Act against the respondents claiming compensation amount of Rs.15,00,000/- on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident. 2. The brief facts of the petition are as under: On 29.8.2017 at about 8.15 p.m. the petitioner was proceeding on a motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-05-EZ- 2204 as a pillion rider and the rider R.Harsha was ridden his vehicle slowly, cautiously on the correct side of Bangarpete-Kolar road, on the way at about 8.15 p.m. near Karnataka Bank ATM, Kolar Town, at that time one Honda CB Shine Motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-07-V-3237 came from opposite direction with high speed in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life and safety of others and dashed against the motor cycle. As a result of the forced impact, the petitioner knocked down and sustained grievous injuries. Immediately the petitioner was shifted to R.L.Jalappa Hospital, Kolar, wherein petitioner took the treatment as inpatient. 3. Further the contention of the petitioner is that, prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy, aged about 19 years, bricks maker and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month. The accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Honda CB Shine motor cycle bearing No.KA-07-V-3237. Therefore, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation. Contending the above facts, he prays to grant for compensation with interest and cost. 4. In response to the petition notice, the respondents have appeared before the court and filed their written statement. 5. The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.1 are as under: The respondent No.1has contended in its written statement that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts. Further contended that the accident not occurred due to the carelessness, rash and negligent riding of Honda CB Shine motor cycle. Further denied the entire petition averments. Contending the above facts, prays to dismiss the petition with costs. Further this respondent has admitted about the issuance of the policy in respect of vehicle bearing No. KA-07-V- 3237 and its validity. 9. To disprove the case of the petitioner and to prove the defence, the respondents have not examined any witness on its behalf. In order to prove the case, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 and he has stated in his evidence by reiterating the contents of petition. On perusal of Ex.P1 is the police intimation, Ex.P2 is the complaint reveals that complaint has been lodged by Ravi, son of Keshaval on 30.8.2017. So, based on the complaint, FIR came to be registered by Kolar Traffic Police in Cr. No.74/2017 against the rider of the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-07-V- 3237 for the offences punishable u/s 279 and 337 of IPC.
texts.arguments: 6.The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.2 are as under: The respondent No.1has contended in its written statement that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts. Further contended that neither the owner of the vehicle nor the jurisdictional police have complied the mandatory provisions of S. 134 and S. 158(6) of the M.V. Act in furnishing the better particulars. Further contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the rider of the motor Shri J.Sarvana vs Shri Ashwatha Gowda on 25 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150170862/ 2 cycle bearing No.KA-05-EZ-2204. Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner as alleged in the claim petition. Contending the above facts, he prays to dismiss the claim petition as against this respondent with cost. Further he argued that, to prove the disablement, the petitioner has examined Dr.Nagaraj B.N. as PW2, who has assessed the disability of left lower limb and 33% and whole body disability is 11%. Further he argued that the petitioner has proved his case as contended in the petition by producing oral and documentary evidence. Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition. 13. Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondents have denied the accident in toto, hence, prays to dismiss the petition. 17. The counsel for the respondents have argued that the accident has not occurred due to the negligence of the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-07-V-3237. But, to substantiate the said fact, the respondents have not led any rebuttal evidence in order to disprove the contention of the petitioner. On the other hand petitioner has proved his case through oral and documentary evidence. 18. In addenda of this, in a claim for compensation U/S.166 of MV Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 (Kusum and others Vs. Satbir and others). 25. The contention of the petitioner is that, he has spent huge amount of Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses. 26. Further contention of the petitioner is that, prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy, aged about 19 years, Bricks maker and earning Rs.20,000/- per month. Due to the accident, he is completely bed ridden and lost his earnings. 28. PW2-Dr.Nagaraj B.N. has stated in his evidence that the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and assessed the permanent disability. According to him, the petitioner has 33% of left lower limb and 11% of whole body disability. So, considering the evidence of PW2 and the cross-examination and the age and avocation of the petitioner and relative disability, if 8% is considered as whole body of disability of the petitioner, it will meet the ends of justice. The petitioner age is already considered as 18 years the multiplier applicable to this age is 18. Thus, the future loss of income workouts as under; Rs.7,500X12X18X8/100=Rs.1,29,600/- 29.
